With a massive NFL event comes numerous NFL betting opportunities for online sports betting . Fernando Mendoza is the overwhelming favorite to be selected No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Raiders, but there are plenty of other DraftKings NFL Draft props than simply who gets selected first. Betting apps have plenty of 2026 NFL Draft props on individual players, positions and teams for prop betting on the NFL Draft. SportsLine NFL expert R.J. White has locked in some of his best bets for the 2026 NFL Draft at DraftKings, including picking star running back Jeremiyah Love, from Notre Dame, to be one of the first four picks in the NFL Draft 2026. White has locked in his five favorite DraftKings NFL Draft prop picks ahead of the opening round on April 23rd. Check them out below. For NFL Draft betting, new users can take advantage of the latest sign-up bonus at DraftKings. Check out our DraftKings promo code review now to see the newest offer and get started. NFL Draft predictions to target Ravens draft offensive lineman first (+130) The offensive line was a major issue for Baltimore last year, and it hasn't gotten any better with Tyler Linderbaum leaving for Las Vegas. Whether it's moving up a bit for Francis Mauigoa or Spencer Fano, taking a plug-and-play interior lineman like Olaivavega Ioane, or even selecting Kadyn Proctor as the heir apparent at left tackle, the Ravens should be using a draft like this that isn't considered stacked with blue-chip talent to stock up on help to address their biggest weakness. We saw a little shift from our initial recommendation to play this at +140 last week, but I believe it should be even odds at least. Trade NFL Draft props at Kalshi. Check out our Kalshi promo code review to see their latest offers. Carnell Tate draft position: Under 7.5 (-105) The market appears to be predicting a little bit of a slide for Tate after the Ohio State receiver was once considered the clear option for the Browns at No. 6. While I believe Cleveland will go with an offensive lineman at that spot, I don't know that Tate gets by the Commanders at No. 7, particularly if Jeremiyah Love and Sonny Styles go off the board in the top five. Tate would be a great running mate and eventual replacement for Terry McLaurin, and receiver is a clear need for Washington. Getting the underdog side of this market while having the potential to hit with either the Browns or Commanders seems like good value. Rueben Bain drafted before Mansoor Delane (-120) This is a head-to-head matchup available at DraftKings that I could see shifting quickly. Teams don't seem to be too worried about Bain's arm length, and on ability alone he has an argument to be taken in the top five in the same tier as Arvell Reese and David Bailey. Delane is probably the best corner prospect in the draft, though a team comfortable with Jermod McCoy's medicals could prefer him, and there is good enough depth at corner that I don't see Delane as a potential trade-up target like Bain could be. Bain's window could legitimately start at No. 4 overall and I can't see him getting past No. 9, while Delane's window starts at No. 8 and probably goes down to No. 12, unless the Cowboys are one of those McCoy teams. That leaves a small margin for Delane to win this matchup. Check out our bet365 bonus code review right now and get their latest sign-up promo. NFL Draft longshot picks Seahawks draft running back first (+380) The defending Super Bowl champions lost their Super Bowl MVP, and White thinks they may turn to the NFL Draft to replace him. The Seahawks declined to franchise tag or re-sign Kenneth Walker III after he rushed for 135 yards in Seattle's 29-13 Super Bowl win over the Patriots. Whether it's with the final pick in the first round or by trading back, White expects Seattle to prioritize a replacement. "No. 32 might be a little high for Jadarian Price, but I think there's a good chance the Seahawks are taking him with their first pick in a different spot," White said. "Running back is their clearest need with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet injured, and we saw how big an impact the rushing attack had in the Super Bowl last year. Seattle has just four picks and will likely prioritize adding more on Draft Day, and those late first-round picks are key for those looking to trade up (maybe for Ty Simpson?) as they come with a fifth-year option. I see the Seahawks making a trade back, then selecting Price in Round 2." Claim the latest BetMGM bonus code. Check out our BetMGM bonus code review now and get it. Jacob Rodriguez drafted in Round 1 (+380) With this draft class being perceived as short on top-tier talent, there is the potential for the back half of the first round to look even more different from consensus mock drafts than recent years. I see logic in examining the Round 1 pick market as a result for longshots we can take a chance on, and Rodriguez fits the bill. He and CJ Allen play a non-premium position at off-ball linebacker but have high floors and reasons to believe each could land in Round 1, especially to teams looking for a piece to come in and make an immediate impact. Rodriguez won a lot of hardware for his collegiate performance in 2025, and in particular, I could see a number of teams in the back half of Round 1 having him higher on their boards than we expect. Lions draft safety first (+3000) Brad Holmes is a best-player-available type of drafter, and with offensive lineman a massive -380 favorite in this prop, I see potential to take a big swing on a lottery ticket play. Detroit's pick at No. 17 is in the perfect range to target an excellent safety class that includes Dillon Thieneman (often tied to the Vikings one pick later) or Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and even though the Lions have one of the best safety pairings in the league when healthy, there are injury concerns around both Kerby Joseph, who reportedly has a serious knee injury that clouds his long-term outlook, and Brian Branch, who tore his Achilles late last season. Every draft has position-team pairings in Round 1 that look surprising on the surface, and this is one that makes some sense. Looking to add some juice to the 2026 NFL Draft? I'm highlighting three intriguing matchups with specific betting lines, including a divisional matchup in the East and a player prop on one of the league's best signal-callers. Here are my three best bets for Week 8 of the 2026 CFL regular season. 2026 CFL Week 8: Best Bets, Picks and Predictions * All odds taken from FanDuel at 4:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, July 23. Calgary Stampeders vs. Winnipeg Blue Bombers Blue Bombers to cover -1.5 spread, -110 The Blue Bombers are undisputed favorites here, and given that the Stampeders are 2-4 and in possession of the worst defense in the league in terms of points allowed (214), one would expect a larger margin in favor of Winnipeg. However, the Stampeders also have the league's best offense (37.7 points per game) and Vernon Adams. Jr. under center, so they can't be overlooked this easily. I'm backing the home favorite on the short spread, though. Winnipeg enters the week at 4-2 and has once again established itself as one of the league's premier teams thanks to its trademark defensive play. The Blue Bombers have been especially tough at Princess Auto Stadium, where crowd noise consistently creates problems for opposing offenses. Calgary has been wildly inconsistent, and that mix of having a prolific offense and defense usually dooms you when you don't have the ball, especially against an offense featuring the likes of Brady Oliveira , Nic Demski , Tim White and a resurgent Dru Brown . The Blue Bombers have won the two games in which Brown has started, and he'll remain the QB1 again here. While Calgary has shown flashes at times, ultimately, the defense won't be able to contain the Blue Bombers, who rank second in the league in points per game (26.0). Toronto Argonauts vs. BC Lions Chad Kelly over 295.5 passing yards, -114 Rather than laying points with Toronto, I'd rather back Chad Kelly 's arm. The veteran is the engine of an offense that ranks first in the CFL in passing yards per game (356.2) and second in total yards on offense (440.3). He's reached the 300-yard threshold in five of his six appearances this season, and the one time he didn't, he still posted 294 passing yards while completing 22 of 33 passes. In short, Kelly has been one of the CFL's most productive quarterbacks this season. This matchup also sets up well from a game-script perspective, as the Lions defense thrives against the run (CFL-best 53.2 yards per game) but struggles massively against the pass (312.6 passing yards per game, 6th). Thus, a scenario in which the Argonauts rely on Kelly to get the win looks completely within the realm of possibilities. The Lions are also expected to turn to Chase Brice under center, which could create extra possessions for the Argonaut offense. But even if this game stays competitive, Kelly should have enough volume to threaten the 300-yard mark. Hamilton Tiger-Cats vs. Montreal Alouettes Tiger-Cats to cover +9.5 spread, -105 There's no realistic scenario in which the Tiger-Cats can be considered favorites in this divisional matchup playing on the road, especially since they won't have Bo Levi Mitchell available due to an ankle injury. Montreal deserves to be favored, but nearly double digits is simply too many points in a divisional matchup. The Alouettes have been one of the CFL's hottest teams, as evidenced by their 5-1 record, but the Tiger-Cats have been competitive even without Mitchell under center. I'm forecasting a win for the Alouettes, but divisional games also tend to be tighter than expected, and Hamilton has every incentive to keep pace in the East standings. With a healthy cushion of 9.5 points, the Tiger-Cats can cover in several realistic scenarios, including a late touchdown in a contest that's otherwise controlled by the Alouettes. Unless Montreal completely dominates from start to finish, Hamilton has an excellent chance of staying inside the spread. More Home Runs. Fewer Strikeouts. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. A $100 bettor is up $7,944 following Warren's futures since this package was created. Click here to learn more about our 2026 Futures Package! D.J. Moore 2026 Over/Under Prediction D.J. Moore is coming off two lackluster seasons by his standards, but a new environment and the opportunity to play with Josh Allen may have created the perfect recipe for an excellent buy-low opportunity. Moore has been seen smiling throughout training camp as he enters 2026 in a dramatically different situation after being traded from Chicago to Buffalo. Instead of playing in an environment where something was clearly not right personally and in a Ben Johnson offense where his target share declined significantly, Moore now gets to catch passes from a former MVP quarterback while reuniting with Joe Brady , his former offensive coordinator in Carolina. The biggest reason to bet Moore’s over is simple: Allen is without a doubt the best quarterback Moore has ever had passing him the ball. Moore has spent most of his career dealing with inconsistent quarterback situations, yet he has still exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in four seasons. He enters his ninth season averaging more than 1,000 receiving yards per season. Moore is also a huge upgrade at the wide receiver position for Allen. The Bills have not produced a 1,000-yard-wide receiver in either of the previous two seasons since Stefon Diggs ’ departure, while their average target depth ranked last in the NFL in 2025. Moore doesn't need an unreasonable target share to beat his season-long receiving-yardage line, but he should command a target share over 20% given the receiver depth in Buffalo. The Bills entered the 2024 season with a new slogan: Everybody Eats. Sean McDermott tried to spin that into a positive after the Bills parted ways with Diggs. However, targets are earned. The “Everybody Eats” slogan was admitting to everyone what was glaringly obvious: There wasn’t an alpha target earner on the roster. In an interview, Ian Rapoport talked about Moore as a breakout candidate for the upcoming fantasy season, but fantasy gamers should be aware that “the Buffalo Bills like to spread the ball around.” Again, this is a mythical statement and is a byproduct of a lackluster receiving room. Diggs was a member of the Buffalo Bills from 2020 to 2023. In those four years, he led all NFL receivers in receptions, was second in targets, and had 28.0% of the Bills' total team targets over that span. Before last season, Moore had four consecutive seasons in which he had over 26% of his team’s targets. In 2021, Brady’s final season as the Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator, Moore had 28.3% of the team's targets and 40.2% of the team’s total air yards. In that season, Moore caught passes from Cam Newton , Sam Darnold , and PJ Walker and still exceeded 1,150 receiving yards. The projections in the Sharp Football Analysis Draft Kit are bullish on Moore joining the Bills. Our projections have Moore projected for 83 receptions and more than 1,100 receiving yards, well over the season-long yardage prop. One of the biggest risks of betting season-long overs is injury. Moore has played every game in the past five seasons and has played 15 or more games in all eight seasons to start his career. Moore has played through injury in the past, which helps give him the opportunity to continue to accumulate volume over the full season. The market may be overreacting to Moore’s 2025 season and overconfident that his decline is age-related. In addition to our projections supporting the over, in the Wide Receiver Trends article, Rich Hribar highlighted that when searching for wide receivers to exceed expectations, one of the more common hits comes from players changing situations, making Moore a solid bet this season. sophomore NFL season as a breakout candidate. Loveland was selected in the top 10 of the 2025 NFL Draft and entered the league with an elite tight end profile and skill set. Loveland started his rookie season slowly as he missed part of training camp with an injury and played a part-time role in the Bears offense in the opening months of the season. He opened his rookie season with just 5 receptions and 54 yards in the opening five games while he was still establishing himself within Ben Johnson ‘s offense and managing an injury. Loveland’s role and production accelerated dramatically as the season progressed. He finished the regular season and playoffs with four consecutive double-digit target games, including a 15-target game in the Bears' playoff victory against the Packers. The late-season production provides a much better indication of what Loveland could look like with a full-time role throughout the entire season. Loveland shared the field with rookie wide receiver Luther Burden for 173 passing plays and generated more targets, air yards, and receiving yards than the hyped second-year receiver. Both Loveland and Burden are projected for increasing roles in Year 2. However, Loveland may still be overlooked. Loveland led the Bears in receiving yards despite only being on the field for 63.8% of the team's dropbacks. With the Bears trading D.J. Moore and not investing much capital into a replacement, there is a significant opportunity for Loveland to increase his target share in an ascending offense. In the final five weeks of the regular season, the Bears had multiple tight ends on the field on 56.9% of the offensive plays. The increase of 13 personnel benefited Loveland the most as he averaged 3.34 yards per route and had 32.4% of the team's targets with three tight ends on the field. Johnson recently did an interview in which he stated that he wants the 2026 Bears to be the highest-scoring offense ever . The Bears have the seventh-most difficult strength of schedule in 2026, after the ninth-easiest last season. Injuries to Coby Bryant and Kyler Gordon are concerning for a defense which is not particularly deep with talent in the secondary, which could force the Bears into more shootouts, boosting Loveland’s ceiling. The Sharp Football Analysis projections have Loveland projected for 90 receptions and 1,068 receiving yards, which is not unreasonable given his late-season production. In the final game of the regular season and two playoff games, Loveland was targeted on 43.3%, 31.3%, and 37.0% of his routes. That is unsustainable, but it indicates that Loveland can push for a 22-25% target share through an entire season. Including the playoffs, Loveland averaged 9.9 air yards per target, which led all tight ends in the league, and gained 20 or more yards on 21.4% of his receptions. The ability to operate deeper down the field and create explosives means that a relatively modest increase in targets can produce substantial increases in yardage. Another important component in Loveland’s ascent is Caleb Williams . Williams registered an off-target throw on 15.9% of his passes targeted at the rookie tight end last season. Entering his third season in the NFL and second season with Johnson, Williams appears more comfortable running the offense than a year ago. Even a slight improvement in accuracy benefits Loveland. Given the way his role expanded throughout 2025, the 2026 season could be the year Loveland goes from promising rookie to legitimate NFL receiving weapon who is mentioned in the same sentence as Brock Bowers and Trey McBride when discussing the league’s high-upside tight ends. For early Week 2 props, I want players with a defined role and a number they can beat without repeating their best game. That starts with a Bills quarterback hosting a Detroit defense that just allowed 410 passing yards, then moves to a pair of rushing props driven by workload. Here are the NFL props I’m targeting for Week 2. NFL Week 2 Player Props to Target Player Prop Projected Line Josh Allen (BUF) Over Passing Yards 220.5 Derrick Henry (BAL) Over Rushing Yards 78.5 Caleb Williams (CHI) Over Rushing Yards 20.5 These projected targets are not posted sportsbook lines. NFL Player Prop Pick: Josh Allen Passing Yards Josh Allen didn’t need big volume to carve up the Texans in Week 1. He completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions in a 36-31 win at Houston. He spread the ball around, too. DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid combined for 230 receiving yards, so Allen isn’t leaning on one target to move the offense. That makes Buffalo a tough team to slow down through the air. The Lions gave up 410 passing yards to Tyler Shough in their opener. He went 35-of-56 with three touchdowns and two interceptions, and Detroit still escaped with a 31-30 overtime win. That yardage came on a heavy workload, and Allen doesn’t need anything close to it. He threw for 334 yards on 29 attempts, which is 27 fewer than Shough. A 220.5 target leaves plenty of room. Allen can fall well short of his Week 1 performance and still cash the over, and he gets the Lions at home on Thursday night. Early Bet: Josh Allen over 220.5 passing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Derrick Henry Rushing Yards Baltimore gave Derrick Henry plenty of work in the opener. He carried 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns in a 41-23 win at Indianapolis. For a yardage prop, the carries matter more than the scores. The Ravens kept feeding Henry in a game they won comfortably, and that kind of volume can get him over this number even if the big runs don’t show up. New Orleans just spent an overtime game trying to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs, without much luck. Gibbs ran 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 5.4 yards per carry. Now the Saints have to deal with Henry. Henry averaged 6.0 yards per carry against the Colts, but this bet doesn’t need that kind of efficiency. Even at 4.0 per carry, 20 attempts would put him over the target. If Baltimore gives him anything close to his Week 1 volume at home on Sunday, 78.5 is a number I’m happy to bet the over on. Early Bet: Derrick Henry over 78.5 rushing yards NFL Player Prop Pick: Caleb Williams Rushing Yards Caleb Williams ran a lot more than usual in Week 1. He carried 10 times for 65 yards and two touchdowns, well above the 4.5 carries per game he averaged last season. That’s the kind of usage you want to see for a quarterback rushing prop. His 2025 numbers already support this bet. Williams finished with 77 carries for 388 yards and three touchdowns over 17 games, which works out to 22.8 rushing yards per game. The 20.5 target sits below that average before Week 1 even enters the picture. The carries could settle back down, and that’s fine. Williams averaged 5.0 yards per carry last season, so he doesn’t need double-digit attempts to reach the low 20s. With the Vikings visiting Chicago on Sunday, I’m taking the over at 20.5. His average last season was already above this target, and he ran more often in the opener.
